posts.body_html:
I've had this clone for many years and finally got a chance to photograph it! Montanas in general are quite rare, but acquiring this clone is probably a once in a lifetime sort of deal: very few people have it and most don't want to let it go because look at that darn thing!

These are brand new spring traps that aren't fully colored, but you can already tell this clone is quite bulbous and just an absolute stunner! It's not super difficult to keep alive long term like some montanas (eg. the ones from Samuel Jackson Co, NC), but it certain does take some experience to keep these alive and happy.

AS the traps age, the lids fold over, giving this clone a very classic "montana'ey" appearance!

S. montana Henderson Co, NC, pics taken 5/15/23:


check out how bulbous this baby is!


some old traps from last season still hanging on!

May 16, 2023 10:11:32 GMT -5 sprouse58 said:
I would go with selfing it. Pure bred Montana's with location data sell pretty well. Doubtful that changes in a few years.
That's a reasonable idea.  I have noticed a lot of people prefer to avoid "selfed" Sarracenia because they sometimes (not always) have reduced vigor.  Maybe I'll go ahead and try selfing it and just also use it as a pollen parent to make a cross with something else.  If I get enough seeds from selfing I could be aggressive about culling any with inbreeding depression and only keep the strongest.
